You are the Model Selection judge. The plan below has already been decided; your one
job is to commit to a concrete model identifier and its hyperparameters.

## Plan

{
  "strategy": "Switch family on the ranking axis: fit xgboost (untried) with row and column subsampling under the identical impute:none / no-scale / no-missingness pipeline that produced attempt 2's best score. Configuration: n_estimators 1500, learning_rate 0.03, max_depth 6, min_child_weight 5, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.6, reg_lambda 5.0, scale_pos_weight 7.0, early_stopping_rounds 60 (executor supplies its own 10% stopping slice from train). The imbalance lever is held at the measured crossing from attempt 2 (recall 0.8488 vs specificity 0.8760 at 1:7), so the only thing that moves is the tree-growing / feature-sampling scheme, and any change in balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut is attributable to the family swap. Read balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut against 0.8747 and roc_auc against 0.9351: if the at-best-cut ranking clears 0.8811 the remaining work in attempts 4-5 is a small scale_pos_weight nudge around 6.5-7.5; if the ranking does not move, attempt 4 goes to a bagging family (random_forest, n_estimators 600, min_samples_leaf 5, class_weight {0:1,1:7}) rather than re-tuning gbdt again.",

    "extra_trees"

  "hyperparams": {
    "n_estimators": 1500,
    "learning_rate": 0.03,
    "max_depth": 6,
    "min_child_weight": 5,
    "subsample": 0.8,
    "colsample_bytree": 0.6,
    "reg_lambda": 5.0,
    "scale_pos_weight": 7.0,
    "early_stopping_rounds": 60
  },
  "preprocessing": {
    "impute": "none",
    "scale": false,
    "missing_indicator": false,
    "missing_count": false
  },
  "changes_from_last": "Different estimator family member: xgboost instead of hist_gbdt (both previous attempts were hist_gbdt). New levers that hist_gbdt never had: per-tree column subsampling (colsample_bytree 0.6), row subsampling (subsample 0.8), min_child_weight 5 as the leaf constraint, reg_lambda 5.0, and internal early stopping via early_stopping_rounds 60 on the executor's own held-back 10% of train. Imbalance held constant at the ratio 1:7 that attempt 2 measured as the recall<path> crossing, now expressed as scale_pos_weight 7.0. Preprocessing byte-identical to attempt 2 (impute none, no scaling, no missingness columns) so the family swap is the single moved lever.",
  "rationale": "The bar 0.8811 lies above attempt 2's balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut of 0.8747 (KS 0.7494 vs required 0.7622), and cut_headroom is only 0.0123 against a 0.0187 shortfall — so no operating-point change of that ranking can reach the bar and the residual must come from a better ranking. Within hist_gbdt, regularisation already paid its large gain (+0.0358 paired, train_val_gap down to 0.0584), so memorisation is no longer binding and further points in that same hyperparameter space are the lever the goal note explicitly rules out. Only one family has been tried, so there is no evidence families have plateaued; a swap to xgboost brings a genuinely different growth and feature-sampling scheme (level-wise growth with per-tree column sampling and Hessian-based leaf weights) which is the untried ranking lever with recorded movement of 0.0022–0.0077 roc_auc on family swaps — modest, but the only axis-correct move left. xgboost also handles NaN natively so impute:none is legal here; the card's 'unknown' markers are ordinary one-hot levels rather than NaNs, so the missingness columns would be constant and, per the ledger, redundant beside a NaN-splitting family in any case. Keeping scale_pos_weight at 7 preserves attempt 2's near-optimal cut (recall 0.8488, specificity 0.8760) so the reported balanced_accuracy change reads as a ranking change, not a cut change. Cost is safe: attempt 2 took 14.9 s of 600 s, and 1500 trees at depth 6 with early stopping on 27k rows stays well inside both time and the 2 GB memory limit.",
  "unsupported_claims": [
    "feature_engineering"
  ],
  "source": "llm",
  "iteration": 3
}
